items.evidence: After page.reload() the spec asserts rules toHaveCount(0) and the empty state is visible (change.diff:136-141), which would fail if the delete mutation never ran.

Criterion 1 is covered at change.diff:127-133 (no rules straight after confirming). Criterion 2 is covered at change.diff:135-141 (after reload: no rules, name input and header still read E2E Tee sale).
No existing page object, scenario or helper covers promotions. The new PromotionPage reuses the PROMOTIONS and ORDERS_SCENARIO constants and copies no existing locator or helper.
No waitForTimeout, sleeps or polling loops; every wait is on a named URL, locator or dialog state.
Imports test from ../../fixtures/test.ts, has no parallel() tag, and writes nothing to the cache, dumps or stored sessions.

Locators use data-test-ids scoped to their containers (rule card, delete dialog). The text locator is used only for the empty state, which has no test id. The position-based hover is forced by the canvas grid, and the row link it reveals is then found by test id.
The spec uses the orders scenario's seeded promotion and creates no data through the API or the UI.
No hard-coded ids; the URL is captured at runtime. Expected values come from PROMOTIONS.catalogue.
Uses the default admin stored session; the ticket names no specific permission, and there is no UI login and no credentials in the spec.
typecheck.txt shows exit 0 with no errors, and the spec lives in e2e/tests/discounts/.
Every locator and multi-step action lives on PromotionPage; the spec only calls its methods and asserts on its fields.
All members are readonly fields initialised from this.page, with constructor(readonly page: Page) {} (change.diff:39).
The spec has // Arrange (change.diff:108) and // Act & Assert (change.diff:124) comments, as the suite does for staged tests.
One test for the one story, split into four test.step stages.
The title describes the behaviour and carries #e2e (change.diff:105).
The header comment at change.diff:93-100 says what the spec covers and why.
All assertions are web-first. The only values read from the page (boundingBox, page.url()) are used for the hover position and a later toHaveURL, not asserted directly.
Uses ORDERS_SCENARIO, PROMOTIONS.catalogue.name and percent. The "Catalog" literal is a UI label, not a scenario value.
No cleanup hooks and no unique names.
No explicit timeouts, retries, networkidle or waitForLoadState.

Relative imports keep the .ts extension. The page object imports expect from @playwright/test, as the existing draftOrderPage.ts and homePage.ts do. The spec takes test and expect only from the fixture.
No any, casts or gql calls.
Comments explain reasons (canvas grid, full-name search, empty state with no test id, why the URL is kept) rather than narrating the next line.

structured_output.summary: Submission f0549153 meets all 23 checklist items (B1–B10, M1–M13). The test checks that the rule removal persisted by reloading the page and asserting the rule count is 0 and the promotion name is still shown. Both acceptance criteria are covered. The new PromotionPage page object follows the suite's conventions, and no existing page object covered this screen. The type check passes. The change also adds a planning document, specs/promotion-rule-removal.md, which no checklist item covers.
